findings.evidence: Original sdkOperations checks before client.connect/callTool, then delegates to the SDK. The SDK has compilation and async request continuations before transport.send, and send serializes the JSON before its unconditional stdin.write. No owned absolute-clock/signal/closed-state guard exists at that final write in this original source. SDK relative timers cannot preempt queued microtasks or synchronous serialization.
findings.qualified_scope_of_existing_checks: workCall has a post-callback check and its abort signal can catch synchronous compilation exhaustion before a later request continuation. That helps but does not cover every later SDK continuation or the serialization-to-stdin.write boundary. The finding does not claim that compilation always causes late dispatch.

finite_static_counterexample.result: The stdio send executes its native stdin.write after the work deadline before a queued timer/post-send observation can run. Any later workflow refusal cannot retract the dispatch. Numbers describe a source-level schedule, not measured runtime.
